title: Impeachment court issues show cause order vs Duterte spox over 'discrediting witness' claim

 Impeachment court issues show cause order vs Duterte spox over 'discrediting witness' claim
 Jaehwa Bernardo ,
 Katrina Domingo ,

 Published November 20, 2026 10:56 AM PHT 
  | 
 Updated November 20, 2026 02:50 PM PHT 
 Sen. Erwin Tulfo, left, and Vice President Sara Duterte's spokesperson Paolo Panelo.  Photos from Wendell D. Alinea, Senate Social Media Unit (Tulfo) and Katrina Domingo, ABS-CBN News (Panelo) MANILA  (UPDATE)  — The Senate impeachment court is set to issue a show-cause order against Vice President Sara Duterte's spokesperson over accusations that several senator-judges attempted to undermine the credibility of one of the defense's witnesses in her impeachment trial.
 During Friday's proceedings, Sen. Erwin Tulfo brought up remarks made by lawyer Paolo Panelo a day earlier, alleging that several senator-judges had attempted to discredit defense witness Rainer Dela Fuente and had shown "bias" against his client.
 Panelo accuses senator-judges of ‘acting like prosecutors’ in Duterte’s impeachment trial  "He's not party to this case pero siya po ang tagapagsalita ng Bise Presidente. Tama po ba 'yon? I mean, parang, I believe parang mayroon hong problema rito," Tulfo said.
 "You are the spokesperson of the Vice President on trial here and then magkokomento ka hinggil sa mga senator-judges, the impeachment court. Para naman wala pong respeto sa, ika nga, impeachment court," he added.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero said Panelo could not be penalized under the Senate impeachment court's sub judice rule, which bars parties involved in the proceedings from making public statements on the merits of the case.
 However, Escudero said the Rules of Court on contempt could still apply to Panelo, prompting Tulfo to propose requiring the lawyer to explain his remarks or summoning him before the court.
 Escudero granted Tulfo's motion to issue a show cause order against Panelo and directed the Senate impeachment court's clerk to serve the order.
 'RIGHT TO COMMENT' In a statement, Panelo insists that his comments were "fair, made in good faith, and did not impede, obstruct, or degrade the administration of justice, and are thus constitutionally protected."
 “The power to punish for contempt does not… render the courts impenetrable to public scrutiny nor does it place them beyond the scope of legitimate criticism,” Panelo said in a statement.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 “Every citizen has the right to comment upon and criticize the actuations of public officers and such right is not diminished by the fact that the criticism is aimed at judicial authority,” he said.
 Panelo said would respond to the show cause order.
 Meanwhile, defense spokesperson Michael Poa said he does not expect the development to affect their panel’s strategy.
 “I don’t think it will affect our strategy at all,” Poa told reporters on the sidelines of the trial.
 “We’ll see how the impeachment court appreciates it,” he said.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 ‘MAINTAIN DECORUM’ But for House prosecutor Rep. Joel Chua, it is “high time” that a show cause order be issued against Panelo.
 “Recently, ang dami niya kasing pinagsasabi na hindi mo malaman kung saan niya hinuhugot… pati ‘yung mga senator judges, inaatake niya. Tapos nag-i-issue siya ng mga mali-maling information. Sabi ko nga kanina, sa 10 sinabi, 11 mali,” he said during a press conference. 
 Prosecution spokesperson Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said that while Panelo does not directly participate in the trial, he has a responsibility as the spokesperson of the respondent.
 “Whatever he says by using that official title reflects the position of his principal,” Adiong said.
 “I guess this is just one way of informing those who are so invested in this trial to maintain decorum… even outside of the court itself. So we have to maintain decorum because this is a sacred constitutional process that we are actually, you know, we are dealing with,” he added.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 On Thursday, the defense faced questions over the credentials and testimony of lawyer and accountant Rainer Dela Fuente, who was called to testify as an expert witness on anti-money laundering matters. However, his direct examination also touched on the report prepared by financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera.
 READ: Defense challenges report alleging Duterte’s P817-M undeclared wealth
 The defense is seeking to refute allegations that Duterte amassed unexplained wealth, failed to fully disclose her assets, and did not divest her business interests while serving as vice president.
